items.title: Christine Jensen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 4, 2024
items.q: Like Ray Wright — I don’t know, or sorry, Ray Ricker — Ray Wright’s dead.

ctx.x: Not always, no. And I’m noticing that too with a lot of that, the Brookmeyer stuff, I’m really caught up in like oh I can see what happens. He started to get really into the composer side of things, not sitting in the band, and then all of a sudden the Vanguard band, how are they going to run this episodic piece, that — someone has to direct it. Same with McNeely — has to direct it from the piano. And there’s just little cues. And so that might be something that you kind of keep in your tool kit as one of the…

some energy. Like Ray Wright — I don’t know, or sorry, Ray Ricker — Ray Wright’s dead. Ray Ricker was at a concert, or he watched a concert the other night and he wrote me a note and he said, “I love your minimalistic conducting. It’s not like you’re like the wind symphony conductors where you have to direct everything.” And I said, “You don’t need to direct everything in jazz.” I mean it depends on context a lot but if the rhythm keeps the pulse of what’s going on, and it’s well rehearsed, you barely have to do…
Yeah. Basie at the piano just like —
